learning: Iteration 6 (7 sensors, 1 cm pitch, 16 mm footprint, 4 cm lead) restored s-bend progress to 0.155, so pitch 1 cm or 1.5 cm is safe and pitch 2 cm or a 2 to 3 cm lead collapses it. The 12 mm footprint at 1 cm pitch is the open question. Watch s-bend progress, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation on all three development tracks, and rms_error for a steady offset.
notes: Single-variable package: the Builder's sensor_size 0.012 m change on the iteration 6 seven-sensor, 1 cm pitch layout. Controller is identical to iteration 6, so footprint is the only change.
rationale: The Builder's proposal is a single-variable test from iteration 6 (score 51.11). Only sensor_size changes, from 0.016 to 0.012 m. The layout stays at seven sensors, 1 cm pitch, x from -0.03 to +0.03 m, y = 0.04 m, with the 0.6 kg mass, 0.11 m track and 0.03 m wheel radius. Evidence: iteration 6 gave s-bend 0.155, oval 0.11, slalom 0.1075 and one line loss per run. Iterations 2, 3 and 5 all collapsed s-bend progress to 0.04 at 2 cm pitch or a 2 to 3 cm lead, while 1 cm and 1.5 cm pitch held 0.155. Footprint at 1.5 cm pitch made no measurable difference (iterations 1 and 4). Footprint at 1 cm pitch is untested, so the controller is kept byte-for-byte identical to iteration 6 (kp 3.0, ki 0, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.6, last_direction line loss, weights x/0.015). That keeps any change in the race attributable to sensor_size. The weight vector already matches the iteration 4 and 6 slope, so no rescaling is needed. Expected result, not measured: s-bend progress at or above 0.15 and line losses at or below 1 per run. If progress falls below 0.11, the 16 mm footprint was needed, and the next lever is the controller's line_loss handling or gains, not geometry. rms_error stayed near 0.03 on all tracks in every iteration, which points to a steady motor-mismatch offset. I am not adding ki in this single-variable test, because integral action on a curved course is untested.
